avoid: Long periods of standing still in line
children.game_version: A 'follow the leader' style where the center couple chooses a funny walk that everyone must copy.

avoid: Deep knee bends during the 'drag' step
seniors.seated_version: Perform the step-touch rhythm with feet while seated; use arms to mimic the promenade motion.
seniors.standing_version: Maintain the two-line formation but use a slower tempo; provide chairs at the end of the lines for resting.
seniors.tempo_and_range: Reduce the travel distance of the promenade.

movement_profile.arms_and_hands: Couples in the center may hold hands (one or both) or move arms rhythmically at their sides.
movement_profile.footwork: In the lines: side-to-side step-touches. In the center: stylized walking, often with a 'drag' or 'slide' feel.
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Two parallel lines creating a central corridor or 'aisle'.
movement_profile.hips_and_torso: Subtle hip sway following the slow tempo.
movement_profile.levels_and_jumps: Low impact; no jumps; movement stays grounded.
movement_profile.partnering: Couples interact primarily during the promenade down the center.
movement_profile.posture: Upright but relaxed, with a slight rhythmic bounce in the knees.

signature_moves.description: Walking down the center aisle with stylized, rhythmic steps while the group watches.
signature_moves.name: The Promenade

movement_profile.tempo_feel: Slow and 'cool', emphasizing the space between beats.
movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Avoid rushing the tempo; the dance relies on the 'slow' feel of the rock 'n' roll beat.

music_profile.musical_form: Standard 12-bar blues or AABA pop structure
music_profile.rhythm_pattern: Slow, steady backbeat with a heavy emphasis on beats 2 and 4
music_profile.sound_description: A mid-tempo rock 'n' roll sound characterized by a walking bassline and a prominent, echoing snare. The music feels 'heavy' and deliberate, inviting a slow, swaying motion rather than fast footwork.
music_profile.vocal_style: 1950s doo-wop or rhythm and blues crooning

basic_steps: Form two lines facing each other (men on one side, women on the other)
Step-touch or sway in place to the slow beat
The lead couple meets in the center at the top of the line
The couple travels down the center aisle with stylized walking or 'elaborate' steps
The couple splits at the end of the line to rejoin their respective sides
teaching.level_notes: The basic in-place movement is beginner-friendly; the center promenade allows for intermediate improvisation.
